question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=1-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{x}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=1-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =1-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y} \\ \frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y} & =1-x \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =2(1-x) \\ (\sqrt[3]{y})^{3} & ={(2(1-x))}^{3} \\ y & =8(1-x)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=8(1-x)^{3}.
$$
